BiblicalUsage: Zaanan was a town in the lowland of Judah, named by Micah when he mourned over the towns of the Shephelah. The prophet says the inhabitant of Zaanan came not forth in the mourning — the town is pictured staying home, shut in, while judgment passed by. It is named once, in a list of towns that would feel the Assyrian advance.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a town named once is not named by accident — Micah's grief covered the small places too. Zaanan reminds me that God's word reaches every street, not only the great cities.
